# Fiscus

> Fiscus is a free and open-source, self-hosted fiscalization service for European tax
> authorities. One deployable service with per-country adapter modules and a
> language-agnostic REST API. Businesses run it on their own infrastructure, so fiscal
> certificates, keys, and invoice data never leave their control. Licensed AGPLv3 —
> free and open source, permanently.

Fiscus is the open-source, self-hosted alternative to commercial fiscalization clouds
(fiskaly, fiskaltrust, DDD Invoices). Instead of sending fiscal data and certificates to
a third-party cloud API, operators deploy Fiscus themselves (Docker) and fiscalize
invoices directly against the tax authority.

Key facts:

- **Status:** in early development (as of 2026). No public source code has been released
  yet. The code will be published at https://github.com/fiscusproject under AGPLv3
  (server) and Apache-2.0 (client SDKs).
- **Audience:** POS, ERP, and SaaS vendors and integrators who need fiscalization —
  developers deploy Fiscus and integrate over its JSON REST API from any programming
  language.
- **Architecture:** stateful service — every invoice processed is stored, and its
  fiscalization status (submitted, confirmed, queued for retry, failed) can be queried
  via the API at any time, giving a durable audit trail. Offline retry and
  flow-control pacing are built on the same invoice store.
- **Planned launch countries:** Croatia (Fiskalizacija 1.0 and Fiskalizacija 2.0 —
  eRačun/eReporting, UBL 2.1, EN 16931), Slovenia (FURS davčno potrjevanje, ZOI/EOR),
  Austria (RKSV, with bring-your-own certified signer such as A-Trust or PrimeSign).
- **Fast-follow:** Spain VeriFactu (AEAT, RD 1007/2023 / Orden HAC/1177/2024) ahead of
  the 2027 mandates.
- **Not planned:** countries that require certified software products (e.g. Germany TSE,
  France NF525, Italy retail, Slovakia eKasa, Serbia ESIR) — Fiscus targets countries
  where compliance means implementing an open protocol, not buying a certification.
- **Name:** "Fiscus" is Latin for the Roman treasury — the root of "fiscal" across
  European languages (le fisc, el fisco, il fisco, der Fiskus). The project is "The
  Fiscus Project"; the software is "Fiscus". Canonical home: https://fiscusproject.eu
